one_line_rationale: Best point-in-time integrity of any family tested (measured after-hours clustering matches theory exactly).

Directly answers the prior fundamentals study's own stated limitation (survivorship from a current-members-only universe) with the SAME economic hypotheses (issuance, earnings consistency) but a 10x-plus broader, survivor-complete issuer set.

Highest raw breadth of the 8-K items tested, but the weakest single economic mechanism because the item code mixes unrelated event types; would need NLP/keyword sub-classification (e.g., isolate M&A agreements specifically) before it is a real candidate, which is a real implementation cost..

SC 13D activism has one of the strongest, most-replicated positive-announcement-return literatures of anything in this scope (Brav-Jiang-Partnoy-Thomas and successors); ~6,500 NEW-stake events/yr (after excluding the /A amendment majority) is a workable, genuinely untested sample..
SEO announcement-return is one of the best-established corporate-finance anomalies; 424B5 gives a workable, moderately-sized, largely unfiltered sample.

Famous 'smart money' mechanism (Griffin-Xu 2009 finds much of the historical hedge-fund-13F edge does not survive out of sample), quarterly-clustered so effective N is modest despite huge raw row counts, CUSIP->ticker->price mapping needed for a large universe with delisted names.

Wide, genuinely untouched cross-section with decent literature support (Boni 2006 and related settlement-failure work), but the ~2-week publication lag and date-only (no intraday) timestamp are real point-in-time weaknesses relative to the 8-K/Form-4 families..

Raw volume is the highest of any item tested, but that is precisely because these are catch-alls; usable only after a real classification effort to pull out buyback/dividend announcements specifically -- rated down on implementation realism for that reason..

High volume but a genuinely weak, well-known-to-be-weak mechanism (proposed, not executed, sales) and a short (2.5-year) fully-electronic history -- the least attractive of the four insider-adjacent families in scope..
One of the most naturally survivorship-RESISTANT designs in the whole scope: react to the notice with a short hold, before the delisting (and the free-price gap) actually happens.

Strong, well-documented mechanism (restructuring/impairment news is bad news) and exactly the kind of firm free price sources lose track of, but under 600 events/year nationwide caps statistical power hard; only worth pursuing pooled with other negative-event families..
Too rare (392/yr) to power a standalone test; valuable only as a label/filter, or pooled with Items 2.05/2.06/3.01/NT-10-K into one 'distress cluster' family..

Too rare to power a standalone test (under 1,000/yr), but among the cleanest survivorship-resistant label signals in the whole scope -- best used as a filter/overlay on other distress signals (1.03, 2.05/2.06, 3.01) rather than alone..

Everything about this dataset is good EXCEPT that quant_v7 already spent a full pre-registered cycle on it and it failed at the 0.70 Sharpe benchmark in both dev and validation with the market hedged out.
